Description

Sprouty proteins are a slower, induced brake on the pathway. Growth factors induce Sprouty genes through ERK, and inhibitors of MEK block this induction [1]. In tumour cells driven by mutant BRAF the Sprouty genes are among the most MEK-dependent transcripts [2]. After stimulation Sprouty2 moves to the plasma membrane and is phosphorylated on a conserved tyrosine, Tyr55. It then binds the adaptor GRB2 and keeps the GRB2:SOS1 complex from being recruited [3, 4]. Its C-terminal proline-rich motif binds the SH3 domain of GRB2 and competes with SOS1 for it [5]. The phosphatase SHP2 removes the phosphate and releases Sprouty2 from GRB2 [6]. Phosphorylated Sprouty2 also binds the ubiquitin ligase CBL, which ubiquitinates it for degradation by the proteasome [4, 7, 8]. With the EGF receptor this has the opposite effect: by holding CBL, Sprouty2 slows the ubiquitination and endocytosis of the receptor and so sustains ERK signalling [7, 9]. Sprouty4 also binds RAF1, but this blocks only RAS-independent activation of ERK [10].
